extracted.intended_audience: small business owners and marketers drafting press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for small-business authors on drafting effective press releases, focusing on what to include, etiquette (dos and don'ts), and how to attract journalists' attention. Emphasizes finding genuine news and following PR etiquette rather than needing a formal PR background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-written and attention-grabbing press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafting a well-written and attention-grabbing press release doesn’t require a Public Relations degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes clear, compelling writing that captures interest; the page implies that good writing is achievable without formal PR training and is foundational to press-release success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find concrete news worth touting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting genuine, newsworthy items is essential — without concrete news, a release is unlikely to attract coverage. The page highlights this as a primary requirement for credibility and media interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn the ins and outs of press release etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning the ins and outs of press release etiquette
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow established dos and don'ts (the infographic referenced) to observe proper format, timing, targeting, and professional norms that improve chances of pickup by journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show credibility and attract busy journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Show off your credibility and attract the attention of busy journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combined goal of newsworthiness, good writing, and proper etiquette is to demonstrate credibility and make it easy for journalists to cover the story; the page frames this as the primary outcome of following the guidance.
